module_title: NETF, NDL, FOSS & NEP 2020's Vision for Educational Technology
introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced DSSSB exams, this level dissects the autonomous bodies proposed by NEP 2020 (like NETF), distinguishes between open-source and proprietary educational software, and explores national repositories.

core_concepts.title: National Educational Technology Forum (NETF)
core_concepts.description:
A landmark creation mandated by NEP 2020. 
- Role: An autonomous body created to provide a platform for the free exchange of ideas on the use of technology to enhance learning, assessment, planning, and administration.
- Function: It will not just buy software; it will articulate the vision for ed-tech, advise state and central governments, and evaluate the efficacy of emerging technologies (AI, VR, Machine Learning) in the Indian educational context.

core_concepts.title: NDLI (National Digital Library of India)
core_concepts.description:
Developed and maintained by **IIT Kharagpur** under the National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT). 
It is a massive virtual repository of learning resources with a single-window search facility. It provides access to millions of books, articles, theses, and manuscripts in multiple languages, catering from primary to post-graduate levels.

core_concepts.title: FOSS (Free and Open Source Software) vs. Proprietary Software
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 heavily emphasizes the use of FOSS to democratize digital education and reduce costs.
- Proprietary Software: Closed source, owned by a company, requires paid licenses (e.g., Microsoft Windows, Zoom, MS Office).
- FOSS: The source code is publicly available to use, modify, and distribute for free. Highly secure and customizable (e.g., Linux, Moodle, Audacity, GeoGebra). India's DIKSHA platform is built on 'Sunbird', which is an open-source technology.

core_concepts.title: NROER (National Repository of Open Educational Resources)
core_concepts.description: An initiative by the Department of School Education and Literacy. It brings together all digital resources (videos, audios, interactives, documents) for school education. It is heavily integrated with the DIKSHA platform to provide Open Educational Resources (OER) that are completely free of copyright restrictions for teachers to use.

important_entities.name: Manodarpan
important_entities.significance: While not a 'teaching' app, Manodarpan is a crucial digital initiative launched alongside PM eVIDYA under Atmanirbhar Bharat. It provides a national toll-free helpline, online chat, and a directory of counselors to address the mental health and emotional well-being of students and teachers, recognizing that digital fatigue and isolation impact learning.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners often ask which institute developed the National Digital Library. Students often guess IIT Delhi or NCERT. The correct answer is exclusively **IIT Kharagpur**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: NETF is the Brain, DIKSHA is the Body
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Understand the difference: DIKSHA is the actual app/platform where content sits (The Body). NETF is the advisory board that researches and dictates *how* technology should be used in the future (The Brain).

exam_strategy_tips: In UGC NET Paper 1, if you are asked to identify 'Open Source Software' used in education from a list, look for names like **Moodle** (Learning Management System), **Ubuntu/Linux**, or **GeoGebra** (Math). Exclude anything made by Google, Apple, or Microsoft.
